## Why does the Workbench's whole-space lint check never run on its own?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Workbench/Maintenance.md] ---
### Space-wide lint

# Space-wide lint
The space-wide lint runs [[API/space#space.lint]] over every page. This reads each page, runs every lint rule and renders its `${…}` expressions and Lua widgets, so on a large space it can take a while. That’s why it never runs by itself: press **Run space-wide lint** when you want it.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Linked Mention.md] ---
### Why?

# Why?
In a traditional notes app, links are one-directional: page _A_ links to page _B_, but page _B_ has no idea. With linked mentions, every link becomes bi-directional. This means:

* You can give a person, project, or concept its own page, and the linked mentions section will automatically collect every reference to it
* You discover unexpected connections between ideas
* Your knowledge graph builds itself as you write

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Baked Sections.md] ---
### Why

# Why
SilverBullet’s most powerful features (`${...}` [[Space Lua]] expressions, [[Space Lua/Integrated Query|queries]], and [[API/widget|widgets]]) are computed live in the editor. That is wonderful inside SilverBullet, but the underlying [[Markdown]] only contains the *source* of the computation. Open such a page on GitHub, in another markdown editor, and instead of a neat table you get to see the raw expressions. This limits your options in further processing markdown (e.g. using some publish tool) or to keep it tool independent.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/CLI.md] ---
### Commands > `lua [code]`

…t starts with a statement keyword (`return`, `local`, `for`, `if`, `while`, `repeat`, `function`, `do`, `goto`, `break`) runs as a script, and you `return` a value to print it. Anything else is evaluated as an expression first, and runs as a script only when it does not parse as an expression. Code never runs twice: when it runs and fails, that error is reported as is, and when it parses as neither, both errors are shown.

Before running, the space catches its index up with recent file changes, so a query sees pages written a moment ago. When that could not be confirmed, a note on stderr says so, for example when the catch-up took longer than 5 seconds. Console output logged during the call (`print`, `console.log`) goes to stderr as well, so stdout holds only the result, also with `--json`.

```bash
sb lua "1 + 1"
# => 2

sb lua "editor.getCurrentPage()"
# => "index"

sb lua 'return 40 + 2'
sb lua --file myscript.lua

# Or pipe from stdin:
echo 'local x = 40; return x + 2' | sb lua

sb lua 'system.reboot()'       # after changing files outside sb (not needed after sb fs write/edit)
sb lua 'space.lint("Page")'    # problems on a page; space.lint() checks every page
```
